No anti-adblock detector or wall is involved:⁠ the page renders its content behind the overlay and no detector script appears in the captured requests. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — jpopsingles.eu serves an inline "AdBlock Detected" detector that builds a randomized-id full-screen overlay, locks scrolling and breaks right-click, and none of the site's existing anti-adblock rules stops it. Three candidate rules (two scriptlets and one HTML-filtering rule) produced no change in any experiment phase while the experiment's own probe reported no anti-adblock detected and no applied rules, so no candidate could be verified and the best scriptlet candidate is handed over for human review.

## Candidate for review

`jpopsingles.eu#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-stack-trace', 'requestAnimationFrame', 'js_func_frame_loop')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: All three experiments came back environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with empty failedCandidateChecks, and the vision review rejected each as 'symptom:⁠ not_resolved' with pageIntegrity intact and no observedDamage. The record contradicts what it captured:⁠ phase A reported an empty appliedRules list although the run's own session lists 21 applied rules on the same page, phase C reported antiAdblockDetected:⁠false although that phase's screenshots show the banner, and two candidates produced byte-identical before/after full-page captures. That points to the candidate not being applied by the adapter's filtering engine rather than to a proven failure of the rule, so it stayed browser-unverified. The mechanism it targets is evidenced separately:⁠ only the detector's inline script uses requestAnimationFrame on this page, and js_func_frame_loop stayed stable across two loads while all other identifiers were randomized.

## Still visible after the rule

- Top center above the post grid, overlapping site header/navigation and first post cards — Visible anti-adblock overlay:⁠ red 'AdBlock Detected' header with white message box 'Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us.' over a dark translucent blackout layer. The site logo, navigation, first post cards ([⁠Single]⁠ PIGMONZ – G.M.B.A and [⁠Single]⁠ ZARAME – Kodou), sidebar Info/Donate area, and Recent Posts are dimmed behind it.
- Top center, overlapping the site header/navigation above the post grid — Prominent anti-adblock banner:⁠ red header reads "AdBlock Detected" and a white box reads "Please consider disabling your ad blocker to support us."; the reporter circled this banner in red.
- Full page behind the banner, including header, navigation, post cards and right sidebar — Dark blackout/dim overlay covers the page content beneath the anti-adblock banner, matching the gated/dimmed page state described by the reporter.

## Missing information

- Scriptlet argument semantics (abort-on-stack-trace / abort-current-inline-script) and HTML-filtering support in AdGuard CLI are not covered by the run's guidance documents: The run's three linked documents (create-own-filters.md, filter-policy.md, CONTRIBUTING.md) served via lookup_rule_guidance give the #⁠%#⁠//scriptlet rule syntax and the $$ HTML-filtering syntax with :⁠contains(), but not the per-scriptlet argument semantics of the Scriptlets library (what abort-current-inline-script's property/searchString actually match against, and what abort-on-stack-trace matches in a stack frame), nor which of scriptlets/HTML filtering the AdGuard CLI adapter actually applies. I needed both:⁠ the candidate had to abort an inline detector that only touches the trapped property from inside a load-event callback, and no document states whether HTML filtering rules are executed by the CLI product or by the experiment adapter.

### Issue URL (Ads) [https://olympustaff.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Folympustaff.com%2F) ### Comment > Aggressive clickjacking/redirection issue on ⁠olympustaff.com⁠. > Whenever I click anywhere on the page, it forces an unwanted redirect to external ad networks (such as ⁠trip.com⁠) through tracking intermediaries. It seems the site uses invisible transparent overlay layers or click-jacking scripts that bypass standard content blocking. > Environment: iOS, using AdGuard for Safari alongside manual DNS protection and a VPN. Please update the filters to block these malicious redirect scripts and invisible overlay elements on this domain. Thanks! ### Screenshots
